content_of_post_to_comment: If you want to argue that AI is no moral patient, does not have a mind, consciousness or mental states… that’s all great, but do NOT overstate your position, don’t treat any of this as a settled issue, it won’t do: you won’t convince anyone by just stating things.
comment: There’s a difference between saying we lack evidence of AI consciousness and having evidence that it’s absent. The first is an epistemic limit; the second is a much stronger claim. What would actually distinguish them?
